subject: Post-call recap: Rooftop Health hosting constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Turner <aisha.turner@rooftophealth.com>, Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@rooftophealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Rooftop Health hosting constraints & next steps

Hi Aisha / Marcus — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next owners. I’ve attached the call notes (PDF) and captured the technical asks below. Please flag anything I mis-stated.

High-level goals (what you said):
- Move inference for patient-facing features to a private deployment (VPC / on-prem) for data residency and regulatory reasons.
- Keep low-latency inference for triage flows (<= 150ms p95 target).
- Minimize egress of PHI outside the US and provide audit logs for 3+ years.

Primary constraints / requirements noted:
- Data residency: US-only region; some workloads must be physically air-gapped for selected clinical trials.
- Network: no inbound internet-facing endpoints into the air-gapped segment; approved outbound proxies or a jump-host/bastion model only.
- Connectivity options: VPC peering or customer-managed VPN to a dedicated Redwood VPC; support for private endpoints (no public IPs).
- Auth & keys: KMS integration (customer-managed keys), HSM/attestation expected for the air-gapped environment.
- Compliance: evidence for SOC 2, pen-test summary, and an audit log stream compatible with your SIEM.
- Ops constraints: customer-controlled patching windows for the air-gapped nodes; we should coordinate maintenance windows.

Open clarifying questions (items we asked you to confirm):
1) Is the air-gap required for all PHI processing or just the subset tied to the clinical trial cohort?
2) Will Rooftop provide a transit VPC and route table, or do you want Redwood to host a dedicated peering VPC?
3) What CA/PKI mechanism do you use for mutual TLS (your internal PKI vs. public CA)?

Proposed next steps & owners:
- Camila (me): share formal post-call notes and a proposed deep-dive agenda (attached) — by EOD today.
- Ben: confirm commercial options (Dedicated capacity pricing & committed discount) — by Tue 6/1.
- Rooftop (Aisha / Marcus): share CISO contact and preferred deep-dive attendees, plus any network diagrams you already have — by Mon 5/31.
- Technical deep-dive (30–60m): propose Wed 6/2 or Thu 6/3 (PST) — we’ll include infra + security + an SRE.

Attachments: 20270528-call-notes.pdf (summary), link to our draft agenda.

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Aisha Turner <aisha.turner@rooftophealth.com>

Cc: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@rooftophealth.com>, procurement@rooftophealth.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 18:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Rooftop Health hosting constraints & next steps

Camila — thank you for the thorough recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: appreciate the bulleting.

Corrections / clarifications:
- The air-gap is required only for the clinical trial cohort (about 5% of requests). The rest of inference traffic can live in a US-only VPC with strict egress controls.
- Rooftop will provide a transit VPC and can set up a managed VPN for peering; our network team prefers not to accept hosted peering on our production slice.

Requests from CISO / procurement: 
- Our CISO (cc’d Marcus) needs a full list of required ports / protocols and any outbound IP ranges to allow through your managed NAT/proxy.
- Procurement needs a draft order form and a tokenized pricing breakdown for Dedicated vs. Private (line items: base infra, committed throughput, support SLA).

We can do the deep-dive Wed 6/2 10:00am PST. Marcus, can you confirm attendees from security?

Thanks — Aisha

Great — thanks for the clarifications Aisha. Answers inline and next artifacts below.

Inline responses: 
- Air-gap scope: understood — air-gapped for the clinical trial cohort only. We’ll propose a hybrid topology with a fully isolated subnet for trial traffic and a US-only VPC for everything else.
- Transit VPC: noted that Rooftop will host the transit VPC and manage the managed VPN. We’ll prepare a peering/VPN playbook for your network team with step-by-step config.

Deliverables we’ll share before the deep-dive (attachments):
- redwood-private-checklist.xlsx — checklist of required ports, CIDRs, KMS integration steps, and patching guidance.
- Proposed deep-dive agenda (agenda section included below) and the SOW owner names.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (30–45m):
1) Introductions & goals (5m)
2) Network topology options & peering/VPN requirements (10m)
3) KMS/HSM integration and key custody (8m)
4) Audit logs, retention, and SIEM integration (7m)
5) Ops/maintenance windows & patching (5m)
6) Commercial summary & next milestones (5m)

Please confirm Wed 6/2 10:00am PST. Also confirm whether the air-gap CA will be Rooftop-managed (we’ll need the CA root for mutual TLS verification).

Thanks — Camila

Attachments: redwood-private-checklist.xlsx

Aisha / Marcus — I’ll join the deep-dive on Wed 6/2 and bring our Dedicated pricing overlay. A couple of quick commercial notes so Rooftop procurement can prepare: 
- We can provide a committed Dedicated pool with a modest term discount if you commit to a 12-month throughput baseline.
- For the air-gapped trial cohort, we typically scope a mixed model: Dedicated capacity pinned to the isolated subnet + burst fallback to hosted (if policy permits). We’ll document the fallback gating and SLAs.

Camila — I’ll share a short pricing spreadsheet by Monday that separates base infra, committed throughput, support SLA, and optional add-ons (longer log retention, extended observability).

Look forward to the deep-dive.

Best — Ben
